en: How to Eat in Xi'an: Begin with Mo
zh: 西安怎么吃：先认馍，再点菜
ja: 西安でどう食べるか：「饃」を知ってから注文する

p.src: To understand a Xi'an table, first notice how mo is used. Wheat-based foods are central to Guanzhong, but that does not make every meal a flour meal or turn a present recipe into an unchanged remnant of one dynasty. Mo is not one standard round bread. Paomo uses firm tuotuomo that can withstand cooking; lazhirou roujiamo commonly uses baijimo. Texture, moisture and baking differ. Distinguishing how each bread is used is more useful than memorising an origin tale.

p.src: Inside the wall, choose an eating context rather than plotting a route through fashionable shop names. Sajinqiao suits an early look at soups and halal snacks. Around Dapiyuan and Xiyangshi, sit down for beef, lamb or sweets and notice how the Hui lanes fit together. Xiaonanmen and Baoensi Street offer a mixed everyday morning market; Yongxingfang is a curated sampler of foods from across Shaanxi. One context is enough for one outing. Recheck stalls and operating conditions near departure.

caption.zh: 城墙内四种用餐环境：清晨的洒金桥、回坊小路、小南门早市与策划型的永兴坊。色圈是选择提示，不是餐馆排名或四站连吃路线。
caption.ja: 城壁内の四つの食事環境。朝の洒金橋、回族街区の路地、小南門の朝市、企画型施設の永興坊を示す。色の円は選択の目安で、店の順位や四か所を回る食べ歩き経路ではない。
caption.en: Four eating contexts inside the wall: early Sajinqiao, the Hui lanes, Xiaonanmen morning market and curated Yongxingfang. The coloured fields guide a choice; they are neither restaurant rankings nor a four-stop eating route.

p.src: For a first bowl of beef-or-lamb paomo, confirm the meat, then ask whether diners break the mo themselves. If so, tear the firm tuotuomo into the bowl as the shop instructs; the kitchen finishes it with meat, broth and vermicelli. Koutang, ganpao and shuiweicheng describe different bread-to-broth relationships, but usage can vary. There is no need to perform expertise: ask plainly for more or less broth, and taste the pickled garlic and chilli separately before adding either.

p.src: Breaking mo is not a pre-meal performance; piece size changes how the bread cooks. Tear the bread into strips, then pinch off pieces roughly the size of a soybean. They need not be perfectly even, and a shop's own instruction takes priority. If fingers or wrists make the work difficult, ask whether the bread can be cut for you. Before the prepared bowl returns to the kitchen, note the table number or how the finished dish will be called.

caption.zh: 泡馍下锅前：把结实的饦饦馍撕成窄条，再掰成小块，碗才送回厨房。块的大小服从店家做法；手指不便可请代切。
caption.ja: 泡饃を煮る前に、硬めの飥飥饃を細い帯へ裂き、小片にしてから器を厨房へ戻す。大きさは店の作り方に合わせ、指が動かしにくければ切ってもらえるか尋ねる。
caption.en: Before paomo is cooked, firm tuotuomo is torn into strips and pinched into small pieces, then the bowl returns to the kitchen. Follow the shop's preferred size; ask for cutting if hand movement is difficult.

p.src: The name roujiamo does not tell you which meat is inside. A common lazhirou roujiamo pairs baijimo with tender braised pork. Halal kitchens may offer la niurou or lamb versions, but these belong to different ingredients and kitchen rules, not a casual substitution. Ask, 'Is this pork, beef or lamb?' rather than inferring from the sign. Eat while the bread still has a crisp edge and before the juices soften its base; state whether you want lean meat or some fat.

p.src: Liangpi is a family, not a single recipe. Mianpi and ganmianpi are principally wheat-based; mianpi may be served with the gluten left from washing the dough, while ganmianpi is generally thicker and chewier. Mipi is rice-based and has another texture. These sheets are cooked or steamed, cooled and cut; they are not raw dough. First ask whether a bowl is rice or wheat, then choose sesame sauce, chilli and garlic water. For sesame, peanut, soy or wheat avoidance, ask item by item rather than judging by colour.

p.src: With belt-wide noodles, the point is the noodle, not counting the strokes in the character biang. Biangbiang mian is one branch of Guanzhong's broad hand-pulled noodles; handmade width varies, and wider is not more authentic. Check whether hot oil is poured over the bowl, whether saozi is included, whether it is dry-mixed or served in broth, and which vegetables and meat are used. Saozi may contain pork, so ask first if avoiding it. Request no or little chilli before the hot oil is poured; it is difficult to reduce the heat afterwards.

p.src: Breakfast reveals how the city starts work more clearly than an evening snack street. Rouwan hulatang is a thick peppery soup; youcha mahua pairs a crisp fried twist with savoury oil tea; zenggao steams glutinous rice with dates. A filled mo travels easily. For two people, share one bowl and add one bread or sweet: that is enough to compare textures without making the morning heavy. Market stalls finish at different times, so an old guide's hour is not a promise. Check same-day operation before setting out.

p.src: Xi'an contains both Hui and Han food traditions, but their labels are not interchangeable. Halal is a religious food practice, not a synonym for vegetarian food or a decorative style. Beef-and-lamb paomo, preserved beef or lamb, and some sweets are common in halal dining. Lazhirou roujiamo normally contains pork; the traditional core of hulutou paomo is pork intestine. Do not bring pork food or alcohol into a halal dining room. When uncertain, ask about ingredients and stock rather than deciding from the district, sign or appearance.

p.src: When two people order in Xi'an, decide which dish will carry the meal's main starch. With a large paomo or broad-noodle dish, add one seasonal vegetable or light cold plate, then one snack only if appetite allows. There is no need to stack paomo, roujiamo, liangpi, noodles and dumplings on one table. Dumplings appear in everyday, halal and banquet settings, so ask about filling and stock. A dumpling banquet is a designed restaurant course, useful for form and service rhythm, not evidence of reconstructed Tang court food.

p.src: Specific questions work better than vague requests: 'Is this pork, beef or lamb?' 'Does the soup contain lard or meat stock?' 'No chilli,' or 'less chilli.' State a severe allergy plainly: 'I have a severe peanut allergy. Even a trace or cross-contact is dangerous.' Carry a Chinese card naming the allergen, cross-contact risk and emergency contact, together with prescribed rescue medication. Vegetarian, halal and less spicy are not allergy statements. If the kitchen cannot give a clear answer, do not eat the dish.

p.src: Arrange a food day as breakfast, one sight, lunch, rest, then dinner. Choose either Sajinqiao or Xiaonanmen in the morning, not both. Give the late morning to one major attraction. At lunch, use a specialist in one staple; spend the afternoon resting at the hotel, walking or taking tea. Sit down for paomo, dumplings, or a dish with one staple at dinner. Add Yongxingfang only to compare foods from across Shaanxi. A queue shows demand at that moment, not age, hygiene or superiority. Look for a focused menu and steady turnover, then recheck operation near departure.
